---
title: "all() on removed NAs is TRUE"
ref: LEN-02
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'all(c(NA, NA), na.rm = TRUE)'
reponse: 'TRUE'
attendu: "`NA`, since no value is known"
versions: "All"
source: "safer-r"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
check <- c(NA, NA, NA)
all(check, na.rm = TRUE)
any(check, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(check, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(check, na.rm = TRUE)
```
:::

## Why

`na.rm = TRUE` removes the `NA`s before computing. When there are only `NA`s, nothing is left, and each function returns its value for an empty vector: `TRUE` for `all()`, `FALSE` for `any()`, 0 for `sum()`, `NaN` for `mean()`.

A check that ran on no known data at all thus turns into "everything is compliant". Nothing signals that the column was entirely missing.

## The remedy

Handle separately the case where every value is missing.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
if (all(is.na(check))) {
  NA
} else {
  all(check, na.rm = TRUE)
}
```
:::
